chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Husayn ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Adha) is among the days in which it is fasted, and the Day of Ashura is the day in which it is not fasted.

key_terms.يَوْمُ الْأَضْحَى: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْعَاشُورَاءِ: The Day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the Day of Adha and the Day of Ashura according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinct jurisprudential status of the 10th of Dhu al-Hijjah and the 10th of Muharram, noting that while fasting is permitted on Yawm al-Adha, it is specifically avoided or prohibited on Yawm al-Ashura. In Shia tradition, this distinction underscores the commemoration of Imam Husayn’s martyrdom, where fasting is often seen as a form of mourning or distinct from the celebratory nature of Eid al-Adha. The ruling reflects the broader principle of distinguishing between days of joy and days of grief in Islamic practice.
